Review.Independence: An independent reviewer subagent that did not see the authoring conversation and did not author the implementation. It was given the contract of revision 1, the complete diff from da60b716a256837acd89601fa8af2e1342c27751 to HEAD 1e86ed6db54ec7c67dbe203c4c286f1ceeaee460, the cited rule files, the receipts run-1 to run-5 with their logs, and the output of status and check. It reviewed the whole diff, recomputed the contract hash, the brief hash, the three definition hashes and the candidate of HEAD independently, compared the title baseline and every test block between the start revision and HEAD programmatically, and verified the run-5 log hashes against the receipt.

Finding.Text: The contract's Change says no test, assertion or helper is changed, added or removed, yet helper.ts grew by about 105 lines: nineteen fixtures formerly file-local in upgrade.test.ts and review-gaps.test.ts were moved into it and exported so the split topic files share one copy, and the constant VERSION was renamed UPGRADE_VERSION (behind and ahead reference the renamed constant). The review verified each moved fixture is otherwise byte-identical to its original at the start revision, the rename is semantics-preserving (both read kernelVersion()), and the suite totals are unchanged at 94 tests and 1407 expect() calls. The deviation is a mechanical consequence of the file split, which the Change also mandates, but the Change's wording does not literally cover it.

CK3's extractor regex matches only double-quoted titles, so the one test with a template-literal title (the parameterized AUTH legacy-fields test serving AUTH-01 and AUTH-02 in receipts-auth.test.ts) is not in the 89-title baseline and its loss, rename or duplication would not fail CK3. The review verified the test is present at HEAD with its legacy-field loop intact. The gap is inherent in the approved check definition, not in the rearrangement.

Review.Adequacy: bun run check is tsc --noEmit over the whole kernel including the twelve rearranged conformance files and the moved fixtures in helper.ts. A pass discriminates A4: a split that lost an import, duplicated an export or broke a moved fixture's types would fail to compile. It cannot show runtime behaviour, test outcomes or speed; those rest on CK2.

bun test --parallel runs the whole suite in the parallel mode the change introduces. The run-5 receipt on the clean final candidate records exit 0 in 122927 ms, and its log, whose hash the review verified, ends with 93 pass, 1 skip (the POSIX-only FL-01 signal test), 0 fail, 1407 expect() calls, 94 tests across 12 files: exactly the totals of the serial baseline in C-0007 run-4, so A1 holds. 122.9 s is under half the recorded serial baseline of 396.6 s (criterion 198.3 s), so A2 holds against the recorded baseline. A lost, broken or parallel-unsafe test would fail the run. It cannot show that the serial form still passes (no check runs it; the contract's D4 accepts this) and cannot show the elapsed time generalises to other hosts or loads (N3 accepts recorded-time evidence judged in review).

The title check compares the extracted double-quoted test titles of all *.test.ts files against the committed baseline and fails on any lost, renamed or added title, which is A3's failure mode; run-5 passed on the clean final candidate with 89 titles, and the log hash matches the receipt. The review verified independently that the baseline equals the sorted title set of the start revision and that all 89 title-to-closing blocks are byte-identical between the start revision and HEAD, and that all 57 documented cases of conformance.md keep a test: 51 by case id in the title, and AUTH-01, AUTH-02, AUTH-04, AUTH-05, AUTH-06 and REL-01 by their bodies, which the review read at HEAD. CK3 cannot show changes inside assertion bodies behind an unchanged title, cannot see the one template-literal title (F2), and does not itself prove byte-identity of blocks; the review's programmatic comparison supplies that.
Review.Rule: The surface grew by nothing: no new command, schema, record kind, skill, tool or validation mechanism; the title baseline is a fixture beside the suite and the parallel flag is the runner's own. The Checks line states the measured parallel duration and that the serial form remains valid. The mechanical split was delegated per the repository rule and the lead verified and committed it: the single implementation commit carries the Change trailer.

Every one of the 57 documented cases keeps at least one test at HEAD; the review confirmed 51 case ids in titles and read the bodies serving AUTH-01, AUTH-02, AUTH-04, AUTH-05, AUTH-06 and REL-01. No case was added, removed, renamed or weakened: the title multiset is unchanged from the start revision and every test block is byte-identical.

No mechanism entered the ledger and none was needed: parallel execution is the test runner's own flag and the title baseline is a fixture of the conformance suite, not a kernel validation. The complete diff touches no file under models/.

approval-1.xml binds the contract hash b209128f... that the review recomputed from the current contract bytes, the brief hash f5cb3173... that the review recomputed from brief-1.html, and the three definition hashes that check reports and that the run receipts carry. The decision is approved by the owner; no approval was inferred and the record holds no conversation.

No kernel-managed path was written by the change: the split touches source under src/conformance/ only, plus package.json and AGENTS.md inside the declared boundary; the records under .grace5/changes/ are kernel-managed and outside the candidate. The review recomputed the candidate of HEAD by the documented rule and it equals 5dbd1035... on the run-5 receipt, which was taken clean; run-2 to run-4 were dirty and count as iteration history only.

The receipts and logs are consistent: the review hashed all three run-5 logs and each equals the receipt's log-sha256; each Result carries the current definition hash; run-5 is clean on the final candidate. Supersession is respected: run-1's CK3 failure, taken before the baseline existed, and the dirty CK3 passes of run-2 to run-4 are history under the highest-numbered-result rule, and run-5's passes on the final candidate are current.

brief-1.html carries the current contract hash, revision 1, writer independent, basis full, and words 763 and checks 3 equal to what check counts; check reports no fidelity defect, so every check row, decision, exclusion and protected path of the contract is present and no finding is open. The approval binds the bytes the owner read.
